Subject: Draft MAP + checkpoint questions

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was impressed by the latency profile and the cost controls. Attached is our initial MAP draft (internal). Two quick asks from procurement before we progress: 1) we need clarity on how pricing discounts are triggered at each MAP checkpoint (what signals / metric acceptance look like), and 2) whether you can provide a variant that assumes a 3-month canary before full ramp (we have compliance gating for Q3).

Can you propose 2–3 pricing variants tied to commit tiers and checkpoint acceptance, and a short acceptance flow we can run by our security/compliance team? Ideally we get a proposal by EOD tomorrow so procurement can start internal approvals.

Hi Sarah — appreciate the context and the MAP draft. I ran this by pricing and legal; below is a compact set of options plus an acceptance flow sketch. Putting Marissa (pricing) and Rishi (commercial approvals) on copy for quick signoff.

Summary (high-level):
- Baseline: PAYG + evaluation credits for 30 days (no commit). No MAP milestone discounts.
- Variant A (Conservative ramp): 6-month MAP, commit to 250k tokens/month by month 4. Discounts: 10% at checkpoint 2 (30 days, basic eval pass), 20% at checkpoint 3 (successful performance SLA + security checklist).
- Variant B (Accelerated ramp): 3-month MAP + 3-month ramp, commit to 500k tokens/month by month 2. Discounts: 12% at checkpoint 1 (functional eval), 25% at checkpoint 2 (SLA met in canary), additional 5% rebate on trailing quarter if usage >= committed volume.
- Variant C (High-commit): 12-month MAP, upfront commit + committed TCO pricing; aggressive discounts (25–35%) applied in tranches aligned to MAP milestones.

Acceptance flow (proposed):
1) Baseline eval (0–30 days): functional smoke tests (latency, top-5 prompt pass rate).
2) Canary (optional 30–90 days): run production traffic at 10–20% on dedicated pool; collect NV and KV cache hit rates, latency percentiles.
3) Checkpoint review: MAP checkpoint doc + runbook (owner: CloudForge eng lead + Redwood AM). Decisions: PASS / PASS WITH REMEDIATION / FAIL.
4) Pricing trigger: discounts apply only on PASS or PASS WITH REMEDIATION if remediation completed within 14 days.
5) Rollback clause: if SLA delta > 15% across 2 consecutive weeks post-checkpoint, Redwood reserves right to revert to prior pricing tier while remediation occurs.

I'll attach a more formal pricing_variants_v3.pdf and a checkpoint_playbook.xlsx in the next message once Marissa and Rishi sign off.

Alex — thanks, this is a clean starting point. A few pricing notes from the commercial desk: 
- For Variant B, swap the 12% / 25% bands to 15% / 22% respectively to better align with our margin targets while keeping the customer incentive to ramp quickly.
- Add a mid-checkpoint health bonus: if average token SLO (p95) improves vs baseline by >10% during canary, provide a one-time marketing credit (not applied to committed usage).
- Checkpoint approvals should include a short acceptance template (2 bullets: metrics + remediation owner + signoff). I added that to a new tab in checkpoint_playbook.xlsx.
- On rollback language: prefer a staged rollback window (30 days) before pricing reversion for enterprise deals; this gives the CS/eng team time to remediate.

If that's acceptable I can greenlight the files for external share. Suggest we offer a slightly enhanced discount at checkpoint 1 for CloudForge (they're strategic) — propose Variant B checkpoint 1 = 18% (instead of 15). Rishi, ok to approve on commercial terms if we limit total FY revenue exposure to X? (I'll DM you numbers).

-Marissa

Subject: Finalized MAP checkpoint flow + Variant B pricing (next steps)

Sarah — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the MAP doc. Per the internal approvals above, Redwood is prepared to proceed with Variant B (Accelerated ramp) with the following agreed items: 

Agreed commercial points:
- Variant B: 3-month MAP + 3-month ramp. Commit: 500k tokens/month by end of month 2.
- Discounts: checkpoint 1 (functional) = 18% off list for committed usage, checkpoint 2 (canary SLA) = 22% off list, plus a 5% trailing-quarter rebate if CloudForge meets or exceeds committed volume.
- Discounts apply to committed usage only; overages billed at standard PAYG.
- Staged rollback: 30-day window; price reversion reserved if remediation not completed within that window. Remediation plan required within 14 days of checkpoint failure.
- Canary: 30 days at 10–20% traffic, with a defined runbook (see checkpoint_playbook.xlsx tab 'Canary-Runbook').

Next steps (timelines):
1) I'll upload pricing_variants_v3.pdf and the three DocuSign exhibits to the HubSpot deal (link below) by EOD today.
2) Procurement to review exhibits — target sign-off by 2025-06-25 to keep Q3 onboarding intact.
3) Post-signature: Redwood will spin a dedicated pool and schedule a kickoff SOW call (AM + Solutions + CloudForge eng).
